## Single-zone heat and carbon monoxide model for the apartment.
## Venting costs heat; sealing costs air.

## Reads the day-by-day design curve. Lows land at 6 a.m., highs at 3 p.m.,
## with a cosine ease between them.

## The medicine cooler: an insulated box, some ice, sixty vials, and a dial
## thermometer. Vials lose potency above 8 C and are ruined by freezing.

## A dead refrigerator. The fridge compartment warms toward the room; the
## freezer holds below zero for a while if you keep the door shut, then its
## ice trays melt one by one.

## What Nick carries. Every entry is one physical thing with its own age, so
## milk taken out of the fridge keeps going off in your bag.
## The five survival meters plus morale, 0..100.
## A battery transistor radio. Stations come and go by day.

## Game time, counted in minutes since midnight at the start of day 1
## (Friday, October 31, 1975).

## Everything on screen: clock, meters, prompts, captions, radio subtitles,
## and the panels (inventory, containers, documents, sleep, pause, endings).

## Builds the apartment shell, its windows and door, the fire escape, the
## airshaft, and a dressed slice of Sullivan Street outside, all from
## data/apartment.json.

## A prop you can pick up (R), carry, and set down on any flat surface (E).
## Big things take both hands: no flashlight while you carry them.

## Box-built geometry and the shared material palette.
## name: [albedo, albedo2, pattern, scale, grain]
## Anything the player can look at and act on. E = primary, R = secondary.

## Builds the apartment slice and drives the light: dawn through the east

##
## Command-line options (after `--`):
##   --smoke             run a scripted playthrough headless and quit (exit 1 on failure)
##   --shots=<dir>       render screenshots from set camera positions and quit

## First-person Nick. Walk, look, interact (E), secondary action (R), carry and
## place props, flashlight (F). No crosshair aim assist; a small dot only.

## Builds each prop from boxes. Every prop's origin is its bottom centre and
## its front faces local +z. Sizes are real 1970s furniture sizes in metres.
## Builds a prop from a layout entry: {"type", "id", optional "prop"/"model"/"kind"/...}.
## "type": "lib" places any baked library prop by name with a behaviour kind.
## Any other type builds that object's gameplay node; "model" swaps its visuals

## A household candle. Light it with a match; it burns down over six hours.

## Opens a container's contents in the HUD. The fridge has two: the fridge
## (E) and the freezer (R).

## The picnic cooler holding Nick's medicine. Two hands to carry.
## Put it out on the fire escape on a cold night; bring it in before it freezes.

## A fixed thing that only answers when you try it: dead TV, cold radiator,
## a light switch that clicks and does nothing.

## The door to the landing. Chained on the inside: it opens a few inches so you
## can look out at the landing. Stepping out ends the slice.

## Carved on Wednesday for Terry. It rots over the first week, one of the
## game's visual clocks.
## A battery transistor radio. E switches it on, the mouse wheel or [ ] tunes.

## The gas range still works: gas mains don't need Con Ed's electricity and the
## pilot lights stayed lit. It cooks, and it heats, and it fills the room with
## carbon monoxide if you shut the windows.
## The bathtub in the kitchen, with a board lid that doubles as a counter.

## A double-hung window. The lower sash slides up to open; open front windows

files.description:
Walks around a built prop and criticizes it.

    blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/critique.py -- PROP [VIEWS_FOLDER] [--out DIR]

1. Measures, by casting rays at the model from front, back, both sides and top:
   - silhouette match against the painted views (IoU per view), if a views folder
     with v_front.png etc. is given;
   - relief: how much real depth the front has (a fully flat front is a smell);
   - painted features: every round part detected in the painting (knobs, dials,
     buttons) is checked for real protrusion, and its depth compared with what the
     part rules say a real one should have;
   - floating or sunken parts: lowest point should sit on the floor (z = 0).
2. Renders a turnaround (8 angles plus 2 close-ups) to _critique.png for a person
   or Claude to look at, and writes _critique.json with the measurements and a list
   of complaints. Read docs/CRITIQUE.md for the review checklist.
imports: from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

files.description:
Geometry metrics of a built prop against its reference views (regression tests, A/B comparisons).

    blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/diag/metrics.py -- GLB VIEWS_DIR [--json OUT]

silhouette IoU per view: the mesh's orthographic outline (rasterised from its triangles, framed to
its bounding box) against the reference view's outline (propkit.hull.silhouette), at the reference's
resolution. 1.0 = identical outlines.
ridge_deg: mean angle between each face's normal and the area-weighted mean normal of the faces
within 3% of the object's size, over faces within 25 degrees of that mean (true edges excluded).
Terraces and grooves raise it; a smooth or cleanly faceted surface keeps it low.

Asset-level geometry regression: rebuild reference assets from their own orders under exp_ names,
measure them (tools/diag/metrics.py) and compare with factory/geometry_baseline.json.

    python3 tools/diag/regress_assets.py [--update-baseline] [--only car,coffee,sofa] [--keep DIR]

Each case must keep its silhouette (IoU no more than 0.005 below the baseline), stay free of folds
(per 1000 faces no more than the baseline + 0.5) and not get ridgier (ridge_deg no more than the
baseline + 0.3). The library, ledger and REPORT are restored and the exp_ outputs deleted afterwards.
About 6 minutes. The fast synthetic suite is tools/test_hull_geometry.py.

Diagnostic renders of a library prop: the same cameras in six modes, to tell geometry from paint.

    blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/diag/render_modes.py -- NAME OUT_DIR [--cams front34,side,...]
          [--glb PATH]   (default assets/props/NAME/NAME.glb, maps beside it)

Modes: clay (no texture), wire (wireframe over clay), albedo (texture only, no lighting), normals
(shading normals as colour), facets (true face normals: shows terraces the smooth shading hides),
depth (distance from the camera), textured (albedo + normal + ORM maps, lit).
Cameras are placed from the object's bounding box, so any prop works.

Human-scale audit of built props: does what we built fit a person?

For each library prop whose kind has handbook contacts (factory/reference_handbook.json), the
contacts are measured on the built mesh and solved like a drawing (propkit/human_scale.py). A scale of
1.00 means the prop is the size a person needs; 1.10 means it should be 10% bigger. Nothing is changed.

    blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/diag/scale_audit.py -- NAME [NAME ...] [--json OUT]

Measures on a mesh: whole width / depth / height (its box), and for a "seat": the up-facing level open to
the sky with the most area in the middle third of the width (top_height) and that level's front-to-back extent
(depth).
imports: from propkit import handbook as HB, human_scale as HS

files.description:
The assembly line: work orders in, finished props and their final renders out, every station timed.

    python3 tools/line.py NAME [NAME ...]         run these orders down the line
    python3 tools/line.py --drawn                 every order built from a drawing (hull and hull_parts lines;
                                                  bench_ orders belong to the benchmark tools)

Stations, in order, for each order (each runs in its own Blender worker; a failed station stops that order
and the line moves on to the next):
  1 intake   if the order names its source sheet ("sheet", "sheet_spec"): the views are cut from the sheet
             (tools/sheet_blobs.py) and any removable guide lines taken out (propkit/guides.py, when the
             order says "guides"); otherwise the views on file are checked
  2 build    geometry, paint, bake, export and the quality gate (tools/factory.py build): ships it to the
             prop library, or flags it for a person
  3 render   the final renders (tools/render_turnaround.py) -> docs/renders/NAME.png
  4 report   factory KPIs (factory/REPORT.md), the line's own summary (docs/renders/LINE.md) and a
             contact sheet of everything that came off the line (docs/renders/line.png)
An order marked "locked" (an approved asset) is not rebuilt: only its final renders are made.
Python's string hashing is pinned (PYTHONHASHSEED=0) so the same orders give the same props.

files.description:
Writes a sheet-set manifest when the set arrives without one (factory/REFERENCE_SPEC.md v2).

    python3 tools/make_manifest.py NAME DIR --type telephone --cm W D H

DIR holds NAME_painted.png, NAME_depth.png, NAME_parts.png and optionally NAME_section.png.
The five views (front, right, back, left, top, left to right) are found by a gutter cut on
the part map, whose background is pure black. Protocol rule 4: before trusting the set, the
painted and depth sheets must line up with the part map; the manifest records how well
(intersection over union of the object masks) and the build refuses a set that doesn't.

Turns painted texture images into seamless tiles and registers them as surfaces.

    python3 tools/make_tiles.py SPEC.json

SPEC: {"source_dir": "...", "surfaces": {name: {"src": file, "box": [x0,y0,x1,y1] | null,
       "kind": "floor"|"wall", "repeat_m": metres per tile, "grid": [cols, rows, inset]?}}}
A "grid" entry splits a swatch board into name_00, name_01, ... Each tile is cropped
square, edge-blended so it repeats without seams, saved to assets/surfaces/<name>.png
and recorded in data/surfaces.json, which the game reads (Geo.mat looks names up there).

definitions.name: seamless
definitions.description:
Cross-fades the tile with a half-offset copy of itself near the edges, so
opposite edges match. Works well on painted, non-photographic surfaces.

definitions.name: period
definitions.description:
Strongest repeat length along axis 1 of a 2-D array, from autocorrelations
of individual rows averaged together (averaging rows first would cancel a
checkerboard out).

definitions.name: periodic_crop
definitions.description:
For regular grids (checkerboards, tiles): crop a whole number of repeats,
measured by autocorrelation, so the tile wraps exactly without blending.
Returns None if no clean repeat is found.

files.description:
Atlas line: an appliance (or any boxy object) from a painted parts atlas.

Jared's atlas sheets lay an object out flat: front panels, sides, top, back, kick
plate, plus loose parts, on a dark background. The machine finds every panel
(`panels`); a work order says which numbered panel is which face, in one line:

    {"front": [[15], [32]], "side": 26, "top": 0, "back": null, "backguard": 1,
     "kick": 24, "burners": 2, "controls": [1]}

front is a list of rows, top to bottom, each a list of panels left to right (a
side-by-side fridge is [[0, 1]]). Panel proportions give the real proportions: the
category gives the height, the front rows give the width, the side panel the depth.
Each front panel is its own slab, standing a little proud with a bevelled edge, so
doors and drawers read as separate parts. Knobs on control panels are found with the
hull line's circle detector and given depth by part_rules (same logic as the TV).

definitions.name: panels
definitions.description:
Every drawn panel on the sheet: [(x0, y0, x1, y1)] in reading order. The
numbering is stable for a given sheet, so work orders can refer to it.

definitions.name: _slab
definitions.description: A panel slab facing -y with the painting on its front (and smeared on its edges).

definitions.name: _face
definitions.description: A thin skin on a body face (side, top, back) carrying that face's painting.

definitions.name: appliance
definitions.description: Builds the object (front faces -y, standing on z = 0). Returns measurements.

definitions.name: _knobs
definitions.description:
Knobs painted on a control panel become fluted cylinders standing proud by
what a real knob of that size would (part_rules), capped with the painting.

files.description: Joins a recipe's parts, unwraps, bakes and exports one prop.

definitions.name: standardize
definitions.description:
Machine-level enforcement of factory/standards.json on the joined mesh, so no
asset needs these fixed by hand: normals outward, seated on the floor (floor-mounted
objects), within its size class's triangle budget, and a texture big enough for the
minimum texel density. Returns (texture size, notes).

definitions.name: fit_texture
definitions.description:
After unwrapping: measure real UV coverage and raise the texture size until the
texel density meets the standard (estimates were wrong by 4x on many-island props).

files.description:
Blade carving for the hull line: find hollows that no outline shows (a sofa's seat).

Silhouettes alone fill a sofa's seat to arm height: in the side view the arm hides it, in the
front view the back cushions fill that outline, from the top it's a rectangle. An engineer
reading the same views does this instead:

- the top view splits into regions (each seat cushion, each arm, the back cushions);
- for a region at the front, the front view shows its top edge as a horizontal line across
  the region's width. A blade pushed in along that line, and one pushed down along the
  region's outline in the top view, meet along the region's real top;
- so the region is cut down to that line, but only if no view's outline changes: every view
  still shows exactly what was painted.

Works on the hull's voxels before smoothing, so the shapes stay soft and painted.

definitions.name: regions

definitions.name: carve

keep: voxels [x (left->right), y (front->back), z (bottom->top)]; sil: {view: (mask, image)}.

files.description:
Cords and cables: build them straight, then curl them along their path.

A coiled phone cord, a lamp flex, a hose or a spring is one construction with different numbers:
  1. straight: the cord laid along a straight line of its path's length - a plain tube, or for a
     coiled cord a helix (coil diameter and pitch from the drawing, kept within human scale), as it would lie on a
     bench;
  2. curl: that straight piece bent along the path it takes in the object (traced from the photo:
     where it hangs from the handset and how it curls), every point carried by the path's local frame;
  3. the wire swept along the result as a tube of the wire's thickness, both ends capped.
Sizes come from the drawing checked against the body (a coil about a finger thick); the path from the photo.

definitions.name: resample
definitions.description: Points every `step` metres along a polyline, and the total length.

definitions.name: frames
definitions.description: Tangent, normal, binormal along a polyline by parallel transport (no twisting flips).

definitions.name: straight
definitions.description:
Step 1: the cord laid straight along z. A coil is a helix of radius coil_r (the radius of the
wire's centre) and the given pitch; coil_r = 0 is a plain straight cord.

definitions.name: curl
definitions.description: Step 2: bend a straight piece (x, y around the z axis, z = distance along) onto a path.

definitions.name: tube
definitions.description: Step 3: sweep a circle of the wire's radius along the points; capped ends.

definitions.name: make_cord
definitions.description:
A cord along `path` (N x 3, metres): straight first, then curled onto the path, then swept.
coil_d <= wire_d gives a plain (uncoiled) cord. Returns (object, report).

files.description:
Geometry building blocks for prop recipes.

Every function adds one part to the current prop and returns the Blender object.
Units are metres, Z is up, the prop's front faces -Y (it becomes +Z in Godot),
and the prop's origin is its bottom centre (floor contact at z = 0).
imports: from mathutils import Euler, Matrix, Vector

definitions.name: box
definitions.description: A box of `size` centred at `loc`. Bevelled by default: nothing is razor sharp.

definitions.name: floor_box
definitions.description: A box resting on z (its bottom at z).

definitions.name: cyl
definitions.description: A cylinder (or cone with r_top) along local Z, centred at loc.

definitions.name: lathe
definitions.description: Spins a list of (radius, z) points around Z: bottles, cans, lamps, bowls, mugs.

definitions.name: tube
definitions.description: A round tube along a polyline (pipes, cords, handles, rods).

definitions.name: rod
definitions.description: A straight cylinder from point a to point b.

definitions.name: label_card
definitions.description: A thin box whose front face (-Y) shows an image material's label (0..1 planar).

definitions.name: planar_uv
definitions.description:
Stores 0..1 planar coordinates (object space) in a 'label_uv' face-corner
attribute so an image survives joining and re-unwrapping. All label coordinates
use the corner domain so parts with labels can be joined together safely.

definitions.name: wrap_uv
definitions.description:
Cylindrical label coordinates around local Z (cans, bottles, jars), stored per
face corner so the seam where the label wraps round doesn't smear. repeat > 1
tiles the label around (short, wide cans); use mats.image(..., extension="REPEAT").

definitions.name: cushion
definitions.description: A soft, rounded block: cushions, pillows, mattresses, folded clothes.

definitions.name: jitter

definitions.name: sag
definitions.description: Pushes the middle of the top surface down (worn seats, old mattresses).

files.description:
Pre-application correction contracts: explain, measure, constrain, or roll back.

This supervises numerical decisions; it is not an LLM or a physical-truth oracle.
Callers supply measurements in declared units and explicit preservation budgets.

definitions.name: assess
definitions.description:
Require the named problem to improve without violating any safeguard.

`improve` names lower-is-better measurements. `limits` maps every safeguarded
after-measurement to an inclusive (minimum, maximum), in the recorded units.
Missing, invalid and non-finite evidence fails closed, rather than guessing.

files.description:
Evidence-first depth estimates and conservative selection of existing relief.

Dimensions remain estimates when source scale/camera orientation is inferred.
No object names, per-image coordinates or runtime LLM calls are used here.

definitions.name: profile_depth
definitions.description:
Side masks share the front's height axis; thin mounting pins are excluded
by the median occupied row width. Opposite-side conflicts stay explicit.

definitions.name: select_relief
definitions.description:
Compare fixed-light height hypotheses with flat paint. Positive lighting
gain prevents an inverted surface winning by fitting negative illumination.

definitions.name: body_hook
definitions.description:
Reuse relief segmentation/displacement, but compare hypotheses first and
suppress regions already owned by separately manufactured components.

files.description: Metric curvature-contrast estimates with explicit calibration uncertainty.

Edge guides for the hull line: annotated copies of the painted views that steer cutting and topology.

An edge guide is the painted orthographic view with coloured lines drawn on it, same view, same
framing (the guide is registered to the painting by its outline here, and the fit is reported):

    red     physical separation between components   -> a full cut / part boundary
    cyan    exterior silhouette                      -> the outline (replaces the painted-mask guess)
    yellow  convex, rounded transition               -> extra local rounding, never a cut
    purple  recessed upholstery crease               -> a shallow pressed groove, never a cut

The guide never becomes texture. From it this module makes a machine-readable mask per view
(one-pixel skeleton lines labelled by class, plus the lines as point lists in JSON) in the
painted view's own crop coordinates, and a mesh hook that applies creases, cuts and rounding to the
dense hull mesh before smoothing and decimation, following the lines' exact curves.

definitions.name: classify
definitions.description: Label image of the guide's coloured lines (0 = none).

definitions.name: body_rows_only
definitions.description: Rows of the object's body (drops painted feet hanging below): last row >= 85% of full width.

definitions.name: register
definitions.description:
The guide's labels in the painted view's silhouette-crop coordinates, and how well they fit.

The guide's object is what its cyan outline encloses; it is mapped onto the painted view's object
box (independent x/y scale + offset). fit = IoU of the two object masks after mapping.

definitions.name: skeletons
definitions.description: One-pixel lines per class (precise curves for Blender), and their point lists.

definitions.name: prepare
definitions.description: Register a guide to its painted view and write the machine-readable mask (PNG + JSON).

definitions.name: mesh_hook
definitions.description:
A hull_prop mesh_hook applying the guides to the dense mesh: creases (and cuts) pressed in along
the exact lines on surfaces that face (and are visible from) that view; rounding near yellow lines.
cuts="groove": a red line is a narrow deep cut in this one surface (a single hull). cuts="structural":
red lines are where separately built parts meet (hull_parts used them to split the parts), so they
are not carved again.

files.description:
Shared dimension/attachment evidence and technical projections of real meshes.

Sections are intersections with the reconstructed mesh, never invented interiors.

definitions.name: export
definitions.description: Use the loaded finished export, not the source paintings, for every line.

files.description:
Extrude line: trim and frames from painted trim sheets.

moulding(...)  a cross-section (drawn on the sheet, or a default for the kind) swept
               straight along a standard 1.2 m length, wrapped with the painted strip.
               Game code places and scales pieces along walls (baseboard, crown, rails).
frame(...)     a painted front (door / window casing, mirror surround, access panel)
               extruded to its real depth, with its opening knocked out.

Inputs are panel numbers from propkit.atlas.panels() on the sheet; nothing is drawn by hand.

definitions.name: section_from_drawing
definitions.description:
The section polygon from a drawn profile: largest drawn region, outline traced
and simplified, oriented so the flat side (the wall) is at y = 0 and the face
points out. Returns None on unusable drawings (explicitly fail, never silently substitute).

definitions.name: moulding
definitions.description: Builds the piece along +x from 0 to PIECE_M, wall at y = 0 (face toward -y), z up.

definitions.name: frame
definitions.description: Extrudes the painted front; a dark opening inside it is cut through.

files.description:
Facade line: a building from one painted front elevation.

    split_sheet(sheet) -> crops of every whole elevation on a facade atlas sheet
    analyse(png)       -> trimmed elevation, window rectangles, storeys, wall colour
    facade_prop(png)   -> the building in the current scene, ready for bake.finish

The elevation is the front. Windows are found where the painting is dark and
rectangular, and are recessed into the wall so they read as openings, not stickers.
A cornice is extruded along the top. Sides and back take the exterior wall surface
(assets/surfaces/ext_*) whose colour is nearest the painted wall, the roof is tar.
Everything is measured from the picture; the only assumption is a storey height.

definitions.name: _xy_cut
definitions.description:
Recursive gutter cut: split a region wherever a full-height column band or
full-width row band is background, until nothing splits. Atlas sheets are laid
out on such gutters; dark shopfronts inside a building never span it fully.

definitions.name: split_sheet
definitions.description:
Whole elevations on an atlas sheet: leaves of the gutter cut that are tall
and big enough to be a building (windows, doors and swatches are smaller).
Returns [(x0, y0, x1, y1)] in reading order.

definitions.name: trim
definitions.description:
Strips background margins from each edge until a row/column is mostly
drawing, so narrow things above the roofline (water towers, chimneys) go too.

definitions.name: _lattice
definitions.description:
Window positions along one axis from the repeat: period by autocorrelation,
opening width and phase from the profile folded over one period.

definitions.name: windows
definitions.description:
Windows from the facade's regularity. Openings are darker than the wall
around them and repeat at a fixed spacing across and up the building, so the
spacing comes from autocorrelation and the opening from the profile folded over
one period. Cells that are not actually dark (signs, blind bays) are dropped,
and the shopfront storey is left as painted. Returns (u0, v0, u1, v1) fractions,
v up. Robust to fire escapes, curtains and paint loss, which defeat blob finding.

definitions.name: facade_prop
definitions.description: Builds the building (front at y = 0 facing -y, standing on z = 0).

files.description: Connected image-curve paths and checked cubic representations; not 3D parts.

definitions.name: paths
definitions.description: Walk actual skeleton adjacency; no straight segments across gaps.

files.description:
Trace internal image boundaries and isolate candidate relief regions.

Regions are observations, not physical parts or assertions of groove depth.
No object vocabulary or geometric templates are used.

definitions.name: trace
definitions.description: Accept linear RGB in the same pixel frame as the foreground mask.

definitions.name: export
definitions.description: Save exact-frame contours, region labels and an inspectable overlay.

files.description:
Construction guides drawn on a painted sheet: read them, then take them out of the painting.

An artist (or ChatGPT) may draw removable guides over the views in one guide colour (cyan on the
updated leg sheet, with a legend): centre lines, outline curves, dashed side profiles, and cross-section
rings (ellipses drawn across a part) meaning "this is round here". The guides carry shape information but
must never reach the model or its paint:

  clean(folder)   every v_<view>.png: guide pixels found by colour (much bluer than anything painted, and
                  bright), saved as g_<view>.png, and painted out of v_<view>.png from the surrounding
                  paint (nearest unguided pixel, then a light blur inside the filled strip)
  ring_band(...)  rows of a view where cross-section rings are drawn: horizontal guide strokes inside the
                  object, away from the centre line. The band from the highest ring to the lowest is round
  round_band(...) the widest band at least two views' rings agree on, with the bottom view's roundness as a check
  round_hook(...) a hull voxel_hook: every slice in that band becomes the ellipse inscribed in the slice's
                  own extent (width from the front, depth from the side), as a lathe would turn it

Intake: crop the views (tools/sheet_blobs.py crop), then
    blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/propkit/guides.py -- clean assets/source_textures/<name>/<part>
and give the order "hull": {"guides": true}.

definitions.name: guide_mask
definitions.description:
Guide strokes plus their anti-aliased fringe: the strict colour test finds the strokes; pixels just
beside them that lean blue at all (paint here is warm: red well above blue) are fringe.

definitions.name: paint_out
definitions.description: Fill guide pixels from the nearest unguided paint, then soften the filled strip.

definitions.name: clean
definitions.description: g_<view>.png from every v_<view>.png's guides; v_<view>.png painted clean. Returns {view: guide px}.

definitions.name: ring_band
definitions.description:
(v_top, v_bottom) of the drawn cross-section rings as fractions of the view's object box (v from the
top), and the ring rows; or None when the view has no rings.

definitions.name: round_hook
definitions.description: voxel_hook: slices with v in [v_top, v_bottom] (v from the top of the object) become ellipses.

definitions.name: round_band
definitions.description:
The round band the views' rings agree on (the widest band two views share); plus whether the
bottom view (if any) is round, as a check. Returns (v_top, v_bottom, report) or None.

files.description:
The reference handbook (factory/reference_handbook.json): what an object type is made of, what its
parts are finished in, and how it meets the human body. It holds no product sizes: the drawing gives
proportions and the body gives scale (propkit/human_scale.py).

    entry = handbook.entry("wall_telephone_rotary")          # or by an alias / category
    handbook.contacts(entry)                                 # how it meets the body
    handbook.material(entry, "hooks")                        # -> (roughness, metallic, class)

Visual hull: a 3D model from orthographic painted views (front, side, top...).

Each view's outline is cut out of a block of voxels; what survives every view is the
object. The surface is extracted with marching cubes, lightly smoothed, decimated,
and every face is painted from the view it faces. One call turns a sheet of views
into a textured prop, so any object drawn in front/side/top views needs no modelling.

    from propkit.hull import hull_prop
    hull_prop({"front": "front.png", "right": "right.png", "top": "top.png",
               "back": "back.png", "left": "left.png"}, height=0.5)

View conventions (as on a typical sheet): front = seen from the front; right = seen
from the object's right side, so the front is on the image's LEFT; left = seen from the
left side, front on the RIGHT; back = seen from behind; top = seen from above with the
front at the BOTTOM of the image. Only front and one side are required.

definitions.name: silhouette
definitions.description:
Mask of the object in a view: differs from the border colour, biggest connected
shape plus small shapes just beside it (legs, feet), holes filled.
Returns (mask, cropped colour image), and the crop box (x0, y0, x1, y1) if with_box.

definitions.name: detect_circles
definitions.description:
Round features in a painted view (knobs, dials, buttons): Hough circles on
edges. Returns [(cx, cy, r)] in pixels, non-overlapping. Radii below 2.5% of the
view's width are edge noise; where circles overlap the larger one wins (a knob's
painted highlights make small false circles inside it).

definitions.name: _sample
definitions.description: mask sampled at normalised coords u (0 left..1 right), v (0 top..1 bottom).

definitions.name: _smooth_contour
definitions.description:
A closed pixel contour (find_contours) as a smooth curve with its real corners kept.

A gentle slope drawn in pixels is a staircase of long treads and 1 px risers; in 3D each tread is
a terrace (lines across a car's hood). Gaussian smoothing of the coordinates along the contour
(sigma ~4 px attenuates a 12 px staircase about tenfold) removes it, and pinning the points where
the outline turns sharply over a few pixels keeps intended corners crisp.

definitions.name: fit_outline
definitions.description:
The mask's outlines as smooth curves fitted through its pixel staircase (_smooth_contour),
rasterised `scale` times finer (even-odd, so holes stay holes). curves=True also returns the
curves ([(row, col) arrays] in the mask's pixel coordinates).

definitions.name: view_distance
definitions.description:
Signed distance (m, negative inside) from the view's fitted outline at the sample grid
us x vs (normalised view coords, same mapping as _sample): [len(vs), len(us)].

Measured exactly to the fitted curves (a KD-tree over points every 0.2 px along them), so
there is no pixel or raster staircase left; the fine raster only says inside or outside.

definitions.name: hull_field
definitions.description:
Signed distance (m, negative inside) of the visual hull: the max over every carving view, each
view's distance computed once on its own 2D grid and broadcast along the axis it looks along.

definitions.name: hull_prop
definitions.description:
convex: fill each outline to its convex shape (boxy objects; dark areas can't
punch holes). paint_only: views used for texture but not trusted to carve (e.g. a
dark back panel on a dark sheet). width_m: the real width (views painted out of
proportion are stretched to it). blades: carve hollows no outline shows (a seat between
arms) from where the views' painted edges meet (propkit/blades.py). voxel_hook(keep, views,
W, D, H) -> keep: a last say over the voxels before meshing (propkit/hull_assembly.py).
mesh_hook(obj): edits the dense mesh before smoothing/decimation (propkit/edge_guide.py).
blur: voxel smoothing before meshing (voxels); large gently sloped bodies (cars) need ~1.5 or their
hoods and sides come out as terraces that catch stripes of paint.
field: "sdf" meshes a continuous signed distance (views sampled between pixels, carving applied
as a CSG difference): no pixel-step terraces. "binary" is the original voxel meshing (blur applies).
revolve: a part whose top view is round (an ellipse once handles/spouts are set aside) is built
as a lathe shape, every slice an ellipse sized by the front and side outlines (propkit/revolve.py).

definitions.name: side_evidence
definitions.description:
How far something sticks out of the front at height v (0 top..1 bottom),
read from a side view: the silhouette's front edge on that row versus the
body's typical front edge. None if no side view.

definitions.name: add_features
definitions.description:
Gives painted round parts on the front view real depth, using part_rules:
each detected knob becomes a ridged cylinder standing proud of the surface by
the amount a real knob of that size would, its cap showing the painted knob.

definitions.name: polygon_hull
definitions.description:
The visual hull built exactly: each view's outline (holes included) extruded into a prism,
the prisms intersected. Flat faces, straight slopes, sharp edges, no voxel staircase; then a
small bevel so nothing is razor sharp. masks: {view: bool array cropped to the object},
conventions as hull_prop (right view: front at the left; top view: front at the bottom).

definitions.name: loft_from_views
definitions.description:
A long, smooth part (handset, handle bar, rail) lofted along x. At every station the
front view gives its top and bottom, the top view its front and back; the cross-section is a
superellipse fitted into that box (exponent 2 = ellipse, higher = squarer, 2.6 = moulded
plastic). Masks are in the object's view frames (front: cols = x, rows = z; top: cols = x,
rows = y with the front at the bottom). Smooth by construction: no voxel or facet steps.

files.description:
Hull assembly line: an object built from its parts, each part a soft hull from its own views.

A parts sheet gives the whole object in five views plus every part on its own (seat cushion,
back cushion, arm, leg...). Each part's own views are larger and cleaner, so each part is
built as its own hull (soft shapes, its own paint); the whole-object views say where each part
goes and how big it is:

- the whole-object front view's top outline has a flat stretch at each end: the side parts (arms),
  giving their width and height;
- the painted seams in the band above the seat split the middle into the repeated parts (cushions);
- a back part's depth comes from its own side view; it stands on the seat deck, a few cm in front of
  the back (the frame keeps a back panel there); a seat part's top is where the blade rule met the
  front-view edge, its thickness from its own front view;
- feet: shapes under the body in the front and side views; each foot's top goes 1.5 cm into the
  body above it, so it is attached by construction. Feet painted on a part's own views are trimmed
  off when the sheet has separate foot views;
- the frame is the whole-object hull kept only under and behind the parts (base, back panel).

No object names: parts are found and placed by those rules, and the order only says which folder
holds which part's views.

definitions.name: strip_feet
definitions.description: Remove shapes hanging below a part's body (painted feet) and save the view.

definitions.name: drop_ground_lines
definitions.description: Delete thin full-width lines (a drawn ground line) from a view, in place.

definitions.name: mirror_views
definitions.description: Views of the mirror-image part (a right arm from a left one).

definitions.name: overlap
definitions.description: Overlap of two [lo, hi] ranges as a share of the shorter one.

definitions.name: confirmed_holes
definitions.description:
Holes that really are background seen through the object. Painted areas close to the sheet's
background colour (black plastic, a dark bezel) are flagged as holes too; a see-through hole must also
show from the opposite side, so where an opposite view exists, a hole counts only where that view (mirrored)
shows background or a hole as well. With no opposite view every flagged hole counts, as before.

definitions.name: paint_views
definitions.description:
Views cropped to the object (the frame texturing.project maps to), paint padded past the outline
with the object's own colours so rounded edges never pick up the sheet background.

definitions.name: orient_top
definitions.description:
Sheets often draw a long part's top view turned sideways (an arm's top drawn wide). If the
view only fits the part's footprint (w across, d deep) when turned 90 degrees, turn it.

definitions.name: fit_to_box
definitions.description:
A rounded hull falls short of its box. On every face that touches a neighbour (or the frame),
stretch the surface out to the box face: measure where the face really is (median of the
surface facing that way, away from the rounded edges) and map it onto the box plane. Outer faces
are left exactly as built. Paint was projected before, so it moves with the surface.

definitions.name: check_gaps
definitions.description:
For each contact, sample the first part's surface facing the second (away from the rounded
edges) and measure how far it is from the second part (0 where it is inside it). Also each
seat/back part against the frame below/behind it.

definitions.name: build
definitions.description: Builds the assembly into the scene; returns a report dict.

definitions.name: colour_model
definitions.description: Colour histogram of a part's own views (non-background pixels).

definitions.name: locate_by_colour
colour_overlap
definitions.description:
Shared share of two colour histograms (1 = identical palettes). Parts painted like the body
(a harvest-gold handset on a harvest-gold phone) can't be found by colour.

definitions.name: match_into
definitions.description:
Where the outline `small` sits inside the outline `big` (both masks): the scale and offset
that put the most of it on `big` and the least outside it (FFT correlation over scales).
Returns (scale, x0, y0, placed mask in big's pixels).

definitions.name: locate_by_subtraction
definitions.description:
The body's own view fitted into the whole-object view (match_into); what the body doesn't
explain is the attached parts. Returns (body box, [part regions largest first]) with boxes as
fractions of the view's object box (u0, u1, v0, v1; v from the top) and each region's mask.

definitions.name: orient_like
definitions.description:
Turn/flip a part's view (0, 180 degrees, mirrored) to best match the same view of the whole
object (outline IoU at the reference's size): sheets draw a part's top view upside down.

definitions.name: body_front_rule
definitions.description:
A body's front view much narrower (for its height) than its back view is a partial view (the
sheet drew only what is left behind the attached parts): carve with the back's outline instead.

calls: np.broadcast_to((zs[None, None, :] >= zcut) & (ys[None, :, None] < yb - OVERLAP), k.shape).copy

files.description:
Human scale: how big a drawn object is, without looking anything up.

The drawing gives every proportion but no size. One table of the adult human body
(factory/human_scale.json) gives size: each object type in the reference handbook lists its
contacts, the places it meets the body (a handset spans ear to mouth, a finger goes into a dial
hole, a seat is at knee height). Each contact measured in the drawing says what the drawing's scale
could be, as a range (people differ, and objects fit them loosely). Several contacts cross-check
each other: the scale is chosen inside the range of the largest group that agrees. A contact
outside it means the drawing is out of proportion there (an artist drew the holes too small), and

      {"name": "plate", "views": "plate", "attach": {"to": "body", "face": "back", "fit": "inside"}},
      {"name": "dial_face", "views": "dial_face", "locate": "match", "attach": {"to": "body", "face": "front"}},
      {"name": "dial_wheel", "views": "dial_wheel", "locate": "concentric", "attach": {"to": "dial_face", "face": "front"}},
      {"name": "hooks", "views": "hooks", "locate": "protrusion", "attach": {"to": "body", "face": "top"}},
      {"name": "handset", "views": "handset", "locate": "residual", "attach": {"to": "body", "face": "left"}},
      {"name": "earpiece", "views": "cap", "attach": {"to": "handset", "face": "right", "at": "top"}},
      {"name": "mouthpiece", "views": "cap", "attach": {"to": "handset", "face": "right", "at": "bottom"}},
      {"name": "cord", "locate": "leftover", "attach": {"to": "handset", "face": "bottom"}}]

How a part is located (where in the object, and how big):
  root        the body's own outline fitted into the photo (hull_assembly.match_into). Every part is
              located in drawing units first; then the scale comes from human scale (the handbook's
              contacts measured in the drawing, propkit/human_scale.py) or from a given body_width_m
  residual    the part sticks out of the body's outline: the region the body leaves over in the photo,
              each box edge from a view where it is visible (hull_assembly.locate_by_subtraction)
  match       the part lies on the body: its painting matched into the photo (propkit.locate)

  protrusion  drawn as part of the parent's own view, sticking out of its outline (cradle hooks on a

  attach      on the parent's face ("at": top / bottom / centre), sized to fit that face
  inset       set into an opening of its parent's front (a CRT in its cabinet): found like match, its face

  leftover    whatever the photo shows that no part explains (a coiled cord): a hull of those regions,

files.description: Small deterministic orthographic/UV rasterizer shared by visibility and QA.

Reconcile: make a painted sheet's views agree with each other before anything is built from them.

Image generators draw pretty sheets that contradict themselves: a top view twice as deep as the side views,
a side view drawn mirrored, printed dimensions that no view matches. Averaging contradictions gives an
object that matches no drawing, so this station measures everything, keeps what agrees and rejects the
rest, and says what it did:

1. Measure every proportion each view shows on the object's core (feet, knobs and cables left out):
   front and back give width/height, the sides depth/height, top and bottom width/depth.
2. Decide each axis. Printed dimensions (the sheet's own numbers) are trusted first; otherwise the largest
   group of views that agree within TOL decides, and the others are outliers.
3. Every view whose proportion is off is not trusted for that axis: the build stretches it to the decided
   size (the hull does this when it is given width, depth and height), and the report says by how much.
4. Orientation: a side view must put the object's front where the top view does (protrusions such as
   knobs stick out at the same end). A side view that matches the top view only when flipped was drawn
   mirrored and is flipped.
5. Opposite views must agree in outline (front vs mirrored back, left vs mirrored right). A view that
   disagrees with its opposite where the opposite agrees with the rest only paints; it does not carve.

Returns the views to build from (flipped copies where needed), the decided size, the views that only
paint, and a report.

files.description:
Relief: the surface inside an outline, read from the painting (2.5D carving: flutes, beads, leaves).

A silhouette says nothing about what the surface does inside it. A painting does, but ambiguously:
darkness means either occlusion (a crease, a groove: light cannot get in) or a surface turned away from
the light (one side of a raised bead). This module separates the two:

1. Outlines from occlusion. "Cavity" = how much darker a point is than its neighbourhood. It traces
   every crease between carved parts, so the creases split the view into regions (a bead, a leaf, a
   flute channel, the strip between two flutes).
2. A shape per region from its outline: a dome (or dish) whose height grows with the distance from the
   region's edge, up to a share of the region's own half width (a bead comes out near a hemisphere; a
   long strip a rounded rib). The creases themselves become shallow V-grooves.
3. Raised or sunk from the shading. A raised dome and a sunk dish have the same outline but opposite
   shading: the dome is lit on the side facing the light, the dish on the side away from it. Each region's
   painted shading is regressed on its dome's slopes; the regions agree on one light direction (taken as
   coming from above, as painters light), and each region is raised if its shading matches the dome, sunk
   if it matches the dish, and left flat (paint only) if the shading says neither clearly.
4. The check: the finished relief, lit by that light, is compared with the painting's shading (correlation
   over the carved area). A relief that contradicts the painting scores near zero or below.

Heights are in the view's pixels until scaled by the view's metres per pixel; every relief is capped at a
share of the object's thinner side. hook(...) displaces a dense hull mesh along its smoothed normals, each
point blending the elevation views by how squarely it faces them (as texturing.project blends paint).

files.description:
Cross-sections inferred from the painting: how round each height band of an object is, without guide lines.

The silhouettes give, at every height, the half width a (front view) and half depth b (side view). They do
not say whether the section there is an ellipse (a turned shaft), a rounded box (a cushion, a car body) or a
sharp box (a square post). One family covers all of these, the superellipse

        |x/a|^n + |y/b|^n = 1        n = 2 ellipse ... n = 4-6 rounded box ... n large: box

so the only unknown per height band is n. The painting decides it by analysis by synthesis: a curved
section lit from the front shades smoothly across its width (brighter where it faces the light, darker
towards its edges), a flat face shades evenly. For each band and each candidate n the brightness across the
width predicted by that section (a constant, plus the section's sideways and facing normal components, any
light) is fitted to the painted brightness; the n that explains it best, by a clear margin over the box,
wins. Fine detail across the width (flutes, carving) is smoothed out first and measured: where it dominates,
the band is "carved" and left to the hull. All four elevations vote (they see the same section from four
sides). Bands with no clear evidence keep the hull's own section: the simplest shape the views allow.

Outputs: a voxel hook for the hull (each slice in a curved band becomes its superellipse, inscribed in the
slice's own extent), a JSON-ready report (observed widths kept apart from inferred n, with the evidence and
a confidence per band), and an overlay per view (the fitted sections drawn as rings in the view's own pixel
coordinates: a picture of the estimate, not decoration).

files.description:
Texture manufacturing: colour a finished mesh from orthographic painted views.

The mesh decides, not the reference sheet. bake.finish later unwraps the mesh into its own UV
atlas and bakes; this module makes what gets baked right:

- every surface point takes a weighted blend of the views, not one view per face:
      weight = facing^4 x visible x resolution
  facing     how squarely the (smoothed) surface faces that view's camera
  visible    1 unless other geometry sits between the point and that camera (ray cast)
  resolution the view's pixels per metre, relative to the best view
- normals used for the choice are smoothed over the surface, so a voxel-carved or decimated
  mesh doesn't flip between views face by face (the patchwork seams);
- where no view sees a point (undersides, inside the cradle) the weight falls back to the
  best-facing view instead of leaving a hole.

project(obj, views, W, D, H, others) -> a material on obj, registered for baking.
views: {"front": path, "back": path, "right": path, "left": path, "top": path} (any subset),
each image cropped tight to the object as seen from that side (front at the image's left in
the right view, front at the bottom of the top view: the hull line's conventions).

area / 3-D area, relative to the median face. Distorted = stretch outside 1/2..2.

files.description:
Split a parts sheet into per-part views and write a hull_parts work order.

    blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/split_parts_sheet.py -- SHEET.png NAME         --rows "assembly:front,right,back,left,top" "seat:front,right,back,left,top"                "back:front,right,back,left,top" "side:front,outer,back,top,bottom" "foot:front,right,top"         --size 1.98 0.86 0.81 [--category sofa]

A parts sheet: the whole object in five views on the first row, then one row per part, each
row's views left to right. Rows are found by the thin separator lines (or, if there are none,
by empty bands); views within a row by empty columns. Each view is saved on black, with any drawn
ground line removed BEFORE holes are filled (otherwise the gap between legs becomes "solid").

--guide EDGE_GUIDE.png [--guide-rows ...] also splits an edge guide sheet into g_<view>.png beside
each view (propkit/edge_guide.py; a view a guide row names "side" is the part's right side).

Background-coloured holes the fill closed are recorded in h_<view>.png (carved solid, never painted).
Writes assets/source_textures/NAME/<row>/v_<view>.png and factory/orders/NAME.json (line
hull_parts, class large, tex 2048). Row names are the part kinds the line understands:
assembly (required), side (arms: outer side view, feet trimmed if a foot row exists), seat, back,
foot. Then: blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/factory.py -- build NAME

Regression tests for the hull builder's geometry (fast: synthetic drawings with known answers).

    blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/test_hull_geometry.py

Each case draws its views, builds with hull_prop (no paint) and checks one property:
  box       stays a box (volume / bounding box), no folds
  slope     a gentle slope drawn at low resolution has no terraces (fitted field at least 2x better
            than binary voxels)
  vase      a round top view is built round (slice circularity) and the lathe carve has no folds
  housing   a C-shaped outline keeps its cavity (front silhouette IoU) and has no folds
  disc      a round front view is built as a lathe about the front-to-back axis
  cord      a cord built straight then curled keeps its turns and coil diameter
Exit code 1 on any failure. Asset-level checks: tools/diag/regress_assets.py.
